content.text:
Act as the review sub-agent for this task.

Role: review only. Do not read files, run commands, edit anything, or use tools. Judge from this description alone, and say where you would want a claim checked before acting on it.

Context: inkling is a Windows Electron desktop app: a React/TypeScript renderer, a Node main process with SQLite, and Effect 4 in the main process. Project rules that matter here: capture must never block on processing; full content must not cross Electron IPC (summaries and thumbnails only); the card grid is virtualized; fetched HTML is untrusted and sanitized; Effect lives only in the main process (one renderer exception, src/lib/ingestion/http.ts); no hardcoded localhost ports or user paths; a logic bug needs a failing test before its fix; prefer the smallest change, and treat rare cases, extra compatibility, and small performance costs as nits. The maintainer does not want scope creep or machinery for its own sake.

Source: a read-only audit by SWE-2 of branch t3/quick-wins-audit, base commit 0e40de9. Goal: small, low-risk fixes that can land now without a product decision.

Already changed in the working tree. Judge each as KEEP or REVERT:
F1. update_item wrote the sourceUrl field with no validation. The other write paths (saveUrl, createQuote, captureUrl) validate it with normalizeHttpUrl. The change: update validates the same way when sourceUrl is provided. Null leaves the stored value alone; an empty string now errors. A regression test was added that fails without the fix.
F2. The reader view rendered the stored sourceUrl as a link href with no scheme check, so a stored javascript: value would be clickable. The change: the footer link renders only for http and https URLs. This was found while verifying the audit, not by the audit itself.
F3. Extension badge: the success timer after a save was never cancelled, so a second save within 1.4 seconds could have its badge cleared early by the first save's timer. The change: cancel the pending timer before arming a new one.
F4. Copy: six places (the extension options page, its script, the background error message, the extension README twice, and STORE.md) say "Settings → Extension". The app's tab is labeled "Browser extension". The change: copy only.
F5. Dead module: packages/ingestion-shared/src/defuddle-config.ts exported DEFUDDLE_VERSION_PIN ("0.19.3", while the root dependency is ^0.19.5) and INKLING_DEFUDDLE_OPTIONS. Nothing imports either. The change: the file was deleted, its re-export removed, the package's own defuddle dependency removed (the root still has it), the lockfile workspace entry updated, and the package description updated.

Open, not changed yet:
O1 [performance, medium size]. Every card-list query (active items, search, Smart Space results) selects the full metadata column. For articles that includes the full extracted HTML and text, and the code parses it for every row. Cards keep only 8 metadata fields, plus a palette and a has-article-content flag. The OCR text column is also selected in full, although cards keep only a 180-character snippet. Options: (a) project only the card fields in SQL, which still makes SQLite read the blob; (b) move article bodies to their own column, which needs a migration.
O2 [latent correctness]. Smart Space kind aliases differ. The renderer maps url to article, embed to video, and tweet to post, on both sides of the comparison. The backend expands only "article". The app's UI never writes a kind into a query (it saves text only), so this affects only imported or hand-written queries.
O3 [dead fields]. durationSeconds, fileSizeBytes, and readingMinutes are in the shared contract and read by card UI (video duration, file-size footnote, reading time). They are never passed through to cards and never written by the main process. Options: delete them, or add producers.
O4 [dead code, about 300 lines with its test]. The extension selection, image, and video capture mappers and their payload types are used only by their own test. The extension currently posts only page-URL captures.
O5 [dead code and doc drift]. src/lib/ingestion/asset-paths.ts (the thumbnail path policy) is imported only by a smoke test. Storage builds its own paths. The ingestion README describes the module as the live thumbnail policy.
O6 [leak, preview mode only]. Preview-mode capture creates object URLs for images and videos and never revokes them.
O7 [correctness, latent]. The file-kind extension lists differ between the renderer's classifier and the storage fallback. svg, heic, heif, and ogv count as image or video only in the renderer; ico and wmv count only in storage. The renderer's kind is normally passed through, so storage is only a fallback. It is unknown whether the image pipeline can decode HEIC or SVG.
O8 [latent]. Imported library archives write source_url with no validation. The display is now guarded by F2. Open question: should import drop or reject invalid URLs?
O9 [trivial]. A benchmark script writes scratch output under a home-directory folder with an old project name. Low confidence that it matters. Skipped so far.

Already checked and clean, no action needed: renderer Effect use is limited to the one allowed file; no Effect.fn in the main process; scoped lint, format, tests, knip, and typecheck pass with the changes above.

Task. For each of F1 to F5 and O1 to O9, give:
- Verdict. For F items: KEEP or REVERT. For O items: FIX NOW, FIX LATER, NIT (dismiss), or NEEDS DECISION.
- For FIX NOW: the smallest concrete change (which files, what changes), whether it needs a failing test first and what that test would assert, and what the change could break.
- For NIT or REVERT: one line of reasoning.
- For NEEDS DECISION: the exact question for the maintainer, and your recommended default.
Then list anything in this description that sounds overstated or misdescribed, anything you would verify before acting, and any issue you think is missing from the list.

Keep the reply under 1,200 words. Use one numbered line per item.

1. **F1: KEEP.** Before keeping it, check one thing: does the renderer's edit form ever send `sourceUrl: ""` (for example when a note or quote is saved with an empty URL field)? If it does, every such save now fails. If so, the renderer should send `null` (or treat `""` as "no change"). Leaving that path broken is not an option. Also confirm that the test fails on `main` because validation is missing, not for an unrelated reason. 2. **F2: KEEP.** It is a real sanitizing fix, and project rules say a check like this earns a test. If the check is inline, move it into the existing URL helper (wherever `normalizeHttpUrl` lives) and add rows for `javascript:`, `file:` and `data:`. The link it guards is only one place `sourceUrl` gets used, though. See "Missing" below. 3. **F3: KEEP.** Check that the error-badge path also cancels the pending success timer. Otherwise a save that fails within 1.4 s of a success gets its error badge wiped. No test is needed. A fake-timer test here would mostly re-check the code's own calls. 4. **F4: KEEP.** Confirm the exact label and casing in the settings tab. Also search `docs/` and the user guides for the same stale string, since only the extension files were listed. The STORE.md change only matters at the next store submission. 5. **F5: KEEP.** Before keeping it, check: - `packages/ingestion-shared` has no other `defuddle` import. Otherwise it now relies on a hoisted copy it doesn't declare. - The extension build doesn't pull defuddle through this package. - No script or doc refers to `DEFUDDLE_VERSION_PIN` by name. Knip won't catch string references. - The `bun.lock` diff touches only that workspace entry. 6. **O1: FIX LATER, as its own PR, measured on a copy of a realistic library.** First check where the 8-field trim happens. If full metadata crosses IPC and the renderer trims it, that breaks a hard rule and becomes FIX NOW. If the trim happens in the main process, the cost is SQLite reads plus a JSON parse per row: real, but it doesn't belong in a quick-wins branch. I prefer (b), a separate article-body column or table. It is bigger than "medium": the FTS triggers, archive export and import, and the reader's fetch path all depend on where the body lives. As a stopgap, `substr(ocr_text, 1, 180)` and `json_extract` for the flag are cheap. 7. **O2: FIX LATER, or FIX NOW if users can type kind tokens.** The claim "the UI never writes a kind into a query" needs checking. If the search parser accepts typed tokens like `type:url` or `kind:tweet`, users can save them as text and the bug is live. The fix would be one shared alias map that both renderer and backend import, plus a backend test that a Smart Space query with kind `url` returns articles. 8. **O3: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Should cards show video duration, file size and reading time? If so, should we add producers now, or delete the fields and their UI until then?" My default is to delete all three, with the contract fields and the card read sites removed in one change. `readingMinutes` would be the cheapest to bring back later, from the extracted word count. Check `docs/product.md` and the design docs first: if they promise any of these, that changes the answer. 9. **O4: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Is selection, image or video capture from the extension on the current roadmap?" My default is to delete the mappers, their payload types and their test, since git history keeps them. First confirm that `capture-server.ts` doesn't validate those payload variants. If it does, removing the types would loosen its validation or break it. 10. **O5: FIX NOW.** Delete `src/lib/ingestion/asset-paths.ts` and its smoke test, and fix the ingestion README line. No failing test is needed. Before deleting, check that storage's own path code has its own containment tests, so this smoke test isn't the only containment check. It could break nothing if typecheck and knip pass. 11. **O6: NIT.** It only affects the dev web preview with sample data, and the leak goes away on reload. 12. **O7: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Should HEIC and SVG be image items, which needs decode or rasterize support for thumbnails, OCR and embeddings, or file items?" My default is one shared extension list: - HEIC and HEIF become files, because Chromium can't decode them. - SVG becomes an image only if it is always shown through `` or a rasterized thumbnail, never opened in a frame or window where its scripts would run. - ICO becomes an image. - WMV becomes a file. - Before choosing for OGV, check whether Chromium still plays Theora. 13. **O8: FIX NOW, with the forgiving default.** On import, run each `source_url` through `normalizeHttpUrl`. If it fails, keep the item and set the URL to null. Don't reject the archive, since losing a user's items is worse than losing a bad link. Test first: import an archive with a `javascript:` `source_url`, then assert the item exists and its `sourceUrl` is null. Possible downside: a hand-edited archive with a non-http link silently loses it. That is acceptable. 14. **O9: NIT.** The path is relative to the home folder rather than an absolute user path, and it's benchmark scratch. Fix it only if someone touches the script anyway. **Overstated or misdescribed** - F2 says the stored value is "found while verifying" and "clickable". How bad that is depends on whether the renderer has a navigation guard (`will-navigate` or `setWindowOpenHandler`) and whether the link goes through `openExternal`. Check both to size it correctly. Either way, it is still the right fix. - O1 calls option (a) a full blob read. That is true for `json_extract` on the metadata column. But if a column is simply left out of the SELECT, SQLite can usually skip that column's overflow pages. So "(a) still reads the blob" depends on which form of (a) is used. - O1 calls the change "medium size". That understates (b) (see item 6). - O2's "only imported or hand-written queries" is unverified (see item 7). - O3's "never passed to cards" should also be checked against the preview seed data. If the seed data supplies these fields, they show up in preview. - "Scoped checks pass" refers to `check:changed` only. That's fine, but say so in the PR body. **Missing from the list** - **Other places `sourceUrl` is used.** "Open original" in the card or detail view, any context-menu "copy or open link", and above all the main process's `shell.openExternal` handler. The http/https allowlist belongs in the main process too, not only in one footer link. If it's missing there, that is the most important fix on this branch. - **Changelog.** F2, and F1 together with it, deserve one Security line in `docs/changelog.md`. - **F1 normalizing.** If `normalizeHttpUrl` rewrites URLs (trailing slash, lowercasing), editing an unrelated field now silently rewrites a stored URL. Check that update only normalizes when the URL actually changed, or accept that behavior on purpose. - **F1's reverse state.** With `null` meaning "no change" and `""` an error, a user can no longer clear a source URL. That's probably fine, but it's a one-way door. Name it.
